title: Implement T60 feedback controller with hard ceiling
description:
Create Source/DSP/FeedbackController.h and Source/DSP/FeedbackController.cpp implementing T60-derived feedback gain for one delay voice.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/ (existing module style, include guards, namespace)
- CMakeLists.txt (for source layout only; do NOT modify it in this task)

Required implementation (restate these formulas exactly in code):
1. T60_voice = T60_global * tailScale_voice.
2. g_requested = 10^(-3 * T / T60_voice), where T is the current voice delay time in seconds.
3. g_final = min(g_requested, 0.985). The 0.985 ceiling is unconditional and applies including during Hold; expose it as a named constant kMaxFeedbackGain = 0.985 and route every returned gain through it. There must be no code path, flag, or Hold mode that returns a gain above 0.985.
4. Guard degenerate inputs: if T60_voice <= 0 or T <= 0, return a documented safe value that still respects the ceiling and never produces NaN or inf.
5. The controller performs no allocation, locking, IO, or string construction in its per-block/per-sample calls. Any smoothing of the T60 target uses a 50 ms time constant and multiplicative (log-domain) smoothing, since T60 is strictly positive.

The files must be standard C++20 only (<cmath>, <algorithm>). Do NOT include any JUCE header.
acceptance_criteria: FeedbackController computes g_requested = 10^(-3*T/T60_voice) with T60_voice = T60_global * tailScale_voice
A named constant kMaxFeedbackGain equal to 0.985 exists and every returned gain is min(g_requested, 0.985)
No code path, including a Hold mode or flag, can return a feedback gain greater than 0.985
Degenerate inputs (T60_voice <= 0 or T <= 0) return a finite documented safe value, never NaN or inf
No allocation, locking, or IO occurs outside prepare()
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: include any JUCE header in FeedbackController.h or FeedbackController.cpp
create or modify Source/DSP/FractionalDelay.*, Source/DSP/DelayTimeController.*, or Source/DSP/DelayVoice.*
introduce any conditional that bypasses the 0.985 feedback ceiling
